item.title: CVE-2021-4034 · PwnKit: Local Privilege Escalation in polkit's pkexec
item.description:
TL;DR: When pkexec is invoked with an empty argument vector (argc=0), an out-of-bounds read treats envp[0] as argv[1], and an OOB write back into envp lets the attacker re-inject GCONV_PATH into the sanitized environment of a SUID-root binary. glibc’s iconv subsystem then loads an attacker-controlled shared library whose gconv_init() executes with EUID 0. No authentication. Deterministic. CVSS 7.8 (High).

1. Context — polkit and pkexec

polkit (formerly PolicyKit) is the authorization framework used by all major Linux desktop environments to allow unprivileged users to run specific commands with elevated privileges according to predefined policies. pkexec is polkit’s SUID-root binary: the only program in this chain that actually carries root privileges on disk.

item.title: CVE-2024-30051 · Heap Overflow in Windows DWM: from an Integer Division Bug to SYSTEM
item.description:
TL;DR: CCommandBuffer::Initialize in dwmcore.dll calls GetBufferSize() twice and truncates one of the results via integer division before passing it to new[], while leaving the second result unmodified for memcpy. The gap is exactly 0x8F bytes. A heap spray of CHolographicInteropTexture objects converts that overflow into a call to LoadLibraryA inside dwm.exe. Requires a local user session. Deterministic. Integrity Level SYSTEM. Patched in KB5037771 (May 2024).

This post documents research conducted as part of my Master’s Thesis in Cybersecurity at UCAM — Universidad Católica San Antonio de Murcia (Campus Internacional de Ciberseguridad), 2025–2026. All testing was performed on isolated virtual machines with no network exposure. The thesis received a grade of 100/100. The exploit analysis builds on the original PoC by Ricardo Narvaja (Fortra/CoreSecurity); the contributions described here — patch diffing methodology, WinDbg dynamic verification, payload logging, and the 50-session empirical heap spray analysis — are original to this research. {.prompt-info }

item.title: CVE-2024-51324 · BYOVD: Three Undocumented Kernel Primitives in BdApiUtil64.sys
item.description: TL;DR: BdApiUtil64.sys creates \Device\BdApiUtil with SecurityDescriptor = NULL — accessible from any process at any integrity level. The termination handler uses PsLookupProcessByProcessId + ObOpenObjectByPointer(KernelMode), bypassing SeAccessCheck unconditionally. ZwOpenProcess is completely absent from the import table. Ghidra analysis reveals two additional primitives with no prior public documentation: arbitrary file deletion (0x80002648) and in-use file deletion with SectionObjectPointer bypass (0x8000264C). No authentication. Deterministic for non-PPL targets. NVD: Awaiting Analysis · ADP CISA: CVSS 3.8 (Low) · CWE-269.

item.title: CVE-2025-55182 · React2Shell: RCE in React Server Components via Prototype Pollution
item.description:
TL;DR: React’s Flight deserializer evaluates any object with a .then method as a Promise, regardless of its actual type. An attacker poisons Object.prototype.then through a crafted multipart POST, forcing the server to execute arbitrary JavaScript via the Function constructor. The result is exfiltrated through the X-Action-Redirect HTTP header as a redirect parameter. No authentication required. Deterministic. CVSS v3.1: 10.0 (Critical).

1. Context — React Server Components and the Attack Surface

React Server Components (RSC) were introduced experimentally in React 18 and stabilized as a production-ready feature in React 19, alongside Server Actions: a model where UI components execute directly on the server and communicate with the client through a custom serialization layer called the Flight protocol. When the client invokes a Server Action, it sends a multipart POST request with a serialized payload. The server deserializes it, executes the action, and streams back the result.
